rationale: Drives where b >= a (gainers) are processed first, sorted by ascending a, since they require minimal initial space and yield net positive free space. Drives where b < a (losers) are processed second, sorted by descending b, to preserve maximum free space for subsequent losers. This is the known optimal greedy for this classic problem.

decision: Direct computation instead of binary search
rationale: Given the fixed greedy ordering, the minimum extra space can be computed in a single O(n) pass by tracking the running free space and finding the maximum deficit. This avoids the extra log factor from binary search and is simpler to implement.
With n up to 10^6, using sys.stdin.read() and splitting is significantly faster than line-by-line input() calls in Python.
